subject: Identity & access cutover sprint — Private Control Plane
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: itops@acme-corp.com, James Park <james.park@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP access for Acme - initial ask

Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and infra teams are ready to start the Private Control Plane cutover but need a clear identity and access plan. Primary asks:

- SAML IdP metadata and assertion flow for SSO (Okta)
- SCIM provisioning mapping for groups/roles (we use group-based role assignment)
- How Redwood plans to map Okta groups to PrivCP IAM roles and service accounts for on-prem connectors
- Timeline for a non-disruptive cutover (we prefer a staged sprint)

Can your team propose a sprint plan with owners, minimal downtime, test accounts, and rollback steps? We also need the list of attributes you need in SAML and SCIM.

I'll attach the baseline security questionnaire separately.

— Samantha
Senior IT Lead, Acme Corp
[attachment: baseline-security-questionnaire.pdf]
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP access for Acme - initial ask

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear list. We've sketched a 2-week cutover sprint (non-peak weekend for migration) and included owners below. High-level plan attached (SCIM-mapping-draft.xlsx, privcp-networking-diagram.png) and the SAML metadata we'll host once you confirm the Okta side.

Sprint highlights: 
- Week 1 (prep): exchange metadata, validate SAML assertions against test tenant, finalize SCIM attribute map. Owner: Dev Patel (infra).
- Week 2 (staged cutover): enable SCIM provisioning for a pilot group, mirror role assignments, run smoke tests, then flip for remaining users. Owner: Soojin Lee (security).
- Rollback: disable provisioning and revert to IdP-only access while we address mappings; we will not change existing Okta groups in your primary tenant until post-cutover validation.

Required SAML attributes: nameID (email), eduPersonScopedAffiliation (or group claims), givenName, familyName, emailVerified, and a custom claim 'priv_role_hint' (optional) for pre-seeding PrivCP roles.

SCIM attributes we want in the mapping spreadsheet: userName, id, active, emails[type=work], groups (memberships), roles (if you supply), externalId. Please review the attached XLSX and mark columns you cannot provide.

Action items from Redwood:
- Dev: build a test IdP assertion endpoint and provide SP metadata.
- Soojin: run threat model against SCIM provisioning flow and share checklist.
- Marcus Lin: coordinate network connectivity tests with Acme network team (I put him on Cc for the diagram).

I'll follow-up with a calendar invite for the kickoff and a Confluence page with the cutover checklist (link below).

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Head of Partnerships (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
[attachment: SCIM-mapping-draft.xlsx]
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP access for Acme - initial ask

Samantha, team —

Technical notes from infra perspective:

1) PrivCP will expose an SP metadata blob for you to ingest into Okta. We'll host the metadata at a short-lived URL during the test window and rotate it after validation.

2) For on-prem connectors, we recommend a service account model using short-lived certs. We will provide a service principal template; Acme should create a namespaced service account in their K8s cluster which the Redwood connector will assume via signed JWT.

3) Role mapping proposal (high level):
- Okta group 'acme-priv-admins' -> PrivCP role 'cp_admin' (full control)
- Okta group 'acme-priv-operators' -> PrivCP role 'cp_operator' (deploy/observability)
- Okta group 'acme-priv-readonly' -> PrivCP role 'cp_reader' (view only)

Limitations: SCIM does not carry fine-grained resource permissions; group -> role mapping is the primary mechanism. If you need attribute-based access (ABAC) we can discuss a custom claim flow.

Network notes for Marcus: please validate that the rendezvous port 8443 from the on-prem Redwood connector is allowed to the private control plane endpoint listed in the diagram. Also ensure the control plane accepts the signed CN from our connector certs.

[attachment: privcp-networking-diagram.png]

— Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP access for Acme - initial ask

Quick security check:

- We'll enforce signed SAML assertions + audience restriction and validate assertion lifetime (<= 5 minutes recommended).
- SCIM will run over mTLS between our provisioning service and your SCIM endpoint; please confirm client cert acceptance.
- Logging: each provisioning action will emit audit events to a tamper-evident log (we can push to your Splunk/CloudWatch as a forwarder).

I will prepare the security checklist items on the Confluence page and mark the high-risk items (group sync conflicts, unexpected role grants). Lauren, can you own the audit forwarding config?

Thanks,
Soojin
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: James Park <james.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, itops@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP access - Okta metadata and certs

Avery / Dev —

Attached: SAML_Metadata_Acme.xml (export from our staging Okta tenant). We exported group claim under 'groups' and can surface a custom claim 'priv_role_hint' if you need it for pre-mapping.

Questions from our side:
- Does Redwood require a specific NameID format (email vs transient)? We prefer email.
- For SCIM, can Redwood accept group-membership push vs. pull? Okta can push groups via SCIM to an endpoint.

We'll plan to run the test assertion on the weekend of Apr 14 (staging). If all good we can plan production flip Apr 21 (non-peak).

— James
IAM Administrator, Acme Corp
[attachment: SAML_Metadata_Acme.xml]
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, James Park <james.park@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: Identity & access cutover sprint — Private Control Plane

Team —

Confirmed. Timeline and next steps:

- Apr 14 (Sat): Staging SAML validation and SCIM attribute validation (pilot group: acme-priv-operators). Owners: Dev (infra) + James (Acme IAM).
- Apr 16–18: Fixes from pilot, update SCIM mapping sheet (we'll record decisions in Confluence). Owner: Soojin + Lauren (audit forwarding).
- Apr 21 (Sun): Production provision for remaining groups if pilot passes. Owner: Avery (program lead) with Acme ops.

Pre-flight check (must be green before April 14):
- Okta has ingested SP metadata and can assert nameID=email (James to confirm).
- SCIM endpoint accepts mTLS client certs and returns 200 for /Users and /Groups (James/itops).
- Network: port 8443 and 5222 (if using connector heartbeat) allowed from Redwood connector egress range. Marcus to validate.
- Audit: forwarding configured to Acme Splunk (Lauren).

If any item is blocked, we will postpone the staging window by one week. Please update the Confluence checklist with results and ping me when staging tests are complete.

Thanks everyone — look forward to a smooth cutover.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Head of Partnerships (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
